newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania Oct inflation falls to 0.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania Oct inflation falls to 0.1 percent.

text.p: Lithuania's monthly inflation rate fell to 0.1 percent in October compared with 0.3 percent in September for a year-on-year rise of 18.6 percent, the country's statistics department reported on Thursday.
Kredyt Bank, which established a representative office in Lithuania ealier this year, is the first foreign bank to be permitted to enter Lithuania's banking market.
The country's parliament lifted a ban on foreign banks in June of this year in response to a banking crisis which rocked Lithuania last year with the suprise closure of two of its top banks.
Lithuania's central bank last Thursday rejected Kredyt Bank's appliactaions on the grounds that it did not meet all of the criteria required to enter the local market.
But it said earlier this week that it would reverse its decision and make an exemption in Kredyt Bank's case as it had applied before the requirements were established.
Kredyt Bank saide it hoped its Lithuanian branch would handle roughly half of the accounts stemming from Polish-Lithuanian trade, which rose last year by 35 percent to $260 million.
